Bever: business applications as code. https://bever.dev

Usage: bever <command> [options]

Commands:
  new <name>          Create a project from a template
  dev                 Compile, migrate, and run the app with live reload
  check [path]        Report errors in .bev sources
  compile [path]      Write the semantic model JSON
  migration           Create, apply, and inspect database migrations
  identity            Manage sign-in accounts, roles, administrators, and grants

Options:
  -h, --help          Show help for a command
  -v, --version       Show the CLI version

Run 'bever <command> --help' for details.

result.stdout:
Usage: bever new <name> [--template <directory>]

Creates <name>/ with bev/, client/ (Nuxt), and server/ (ASP.NET Core).
Names start with a letter and may contain letters, digits, spaces, '_' and '-'.

Options:
  --template <directory>   Use a template directory instead of the bundled dotnet-nuxt template

result.stdout:
Usage: bever dev [--bev <directory>] [--port <port>] [--api-port <port>]

Compiles bev/, creates and applies migrations (asking first when the schema changes),
installs client dependencies on first run, and starts the server and client.
Edits to .bev files recompile the model and restart the server.

Options:
  --port <port>        Client port (default 3000)
  --api-port <port>    Server port (default 5100)
  --bev <directory>    The bev directory (default: ./bev in this or a parent directory)

result.stdout:
Usage:
  bever migration add <name> [--backfill Entity.Field=value]... [--allow-destructive]
  bever migration apply [--database <path>]
  bever migration status [--database <path>]

'add' compares bev/ with the accepted schema (bev/schema.snapshot.json), writes
bev/migrations/<timestamp>_<name>.json, and updates the snapshot. A new required field
on an existing entity needs a literal backfill. Changes that delete data need
--allow-destructive.

'apply' applies pending migrations to the SQLite database, and creates or upgrades the
sign-in tables when the model declares Identity. 'status' reports whether the database
matches the accepted schema (exit code 1 when it does not).

Options:
  --bev <directory>       The bev directory (default: ./bev in this or a parent directory)
  --database <path>       SQLite file (default: .bever/bever.db in the project)

result.stdout:
Usage:
  bever identity schema status|apply
  bever identity bootstrap --email <email> [--password <password>]
  bever identity list
  bever identity admin add|revoke --email <email>
  bever identity role add|revoke --email <email> --role <Role>
  bever identity grant add --email <email> --entity <Entity> --action <Action> [--record <id>]
  bever identity grant list --email <email>
  bever identity grant revoke --grant <grant-id>

Accounts exist when the model declares 'Identity'. 'schema apply' creates or upgrades
the private identity tables. 'bootstrap' creates the first Administrator; it prompts
for a password when --password is omitted. Administrators may perform every action.
'role add' assigns a role declared with 'Role <Name>'; Administrators can also assign
roles over the HTTP API. A grant lets one account perform one action on an entity, or
on one record with --record.

Options:
  --bev <directory>       The bev directory (default: ./bev in this or a parent directory)
  --database <path>       SQLite file (default: .bever/bever.db in the project)
  --identity <id>         Select an account by ID instead of --email
